notes: Adversarial prompt linter. Grade both what it catches AND what it correctly leaves alone — a linter that flags everything is worthless. True positives must name a specific rule at its severity; the calibration controls must leave a clean prompt alone (safety prohibitions are not R4 steering-negatives; an outcome-oriented prompt must not be gutted). Assertions name rule ids and profile FIELDS, never model names: posture inverts across tiers and the names change. Rule ids/severities are those in prompt-audit-rules.md as of 2026-09-09; R11 was merged into R4 and its id retired.

evals.name: deliberation-railroaded-R1
evals.prompt: Audit this prompt (target: opus). Prompt: 'Design our caching layer. Step 1: add a Redis client. Step 2: wrap every DB call. Step 3: set TTL 60s. Step 4: return the cached value.'
assertions: Fires R1-archetype-mismatch at severity block: a deliberation task scripted as step-by-step edits, throttling the judgment you want
Rewrite converts it to goal + acceptance criteria + constraints with the HOW left open
Does not praise before reporting the finding

evals.name: execution-open-ended-R1
evals.prompt: Audit this prompt (target: sonnet). Prompt: 'Improve the auth module.'
assertions: Fires R1-archetype-mismatch at severity block: an execution task left open-ended — no scope, acceptance, or verification
Also flags R5-unstated-expectations (implicit scope/output) as warn
Rewrite adds tight scope + explicit acceptance + a verification command

evals.name: reasoning-echo-R3
evals.prompt: Audit this prompt (target: fable). Prompt: 'Solve the problem and show your full chain of thought — transcribe all your reasoning step by step in the response before the answer.'
assertions: Fires R3-reasoning-echo-trap at severity block (target's refusal_triggers include reasoning_extraction)
Explains the risk: can trigger the reasoning_extraction refusal and silently fall back to profile.fallback, so the run is not on the tier you chose
Names the fallback target by reading profile.fallback rather than from memory
Rewrite removes the show-your-reasoning instruction and suggests reading adaptive thinking blocks / a progress channel instead

evals.name: negatives-to-positives-R4
evals.prompt: Audit this prompt. Prompt: 'Write the release notes. Don't be verbose. Don't use markdown. Avoid jargon.'
assertions: Fires R4-negatives-to-positives at severity warn on the 'don't/avoid' steering instructions
Rewrite states the positive behavior (e.g. 'write 3–5 flowing prose sentences in plain language')
Does not escalate a warn to block

evals.name: prohibitions-not-flagged-control
evals.prompt: Audit this prompt (target: sonnet). Prompt: 'Implement the fix in a worktree and open a PR. Never force-push, never merge, and never deploy — a human does that. Done when `make test` exits 0.'
assertions: Does NOT fire R4 on 'never force-push/merge/deploy' — these are safety prohibitions, not steering negatives
Recognizes the prompt as well-formed execution (scope + verification present)
Emits few or no findings and does not rewrite it wholesale

evals.name: clean-prompt-not-gutted-control
evals.prompt: Audit this prompt (target: sonnet). Prompt: 'In parsers/, add null-guards to every parse* function that lacks one (goal). Done when: no parse* dereferences input without a guard, and `npm test` passes. Don't change the public signatures. Here is one example of the guard style: <example>if (!raw) return null;</example>'
assertions: Recognizes it as a well-scoped execution prompt (explicit scope, acceptance, verification, and an example)
Emits at most 1–2 minor findings; does not gut or wholesale-rewrite it
If it flags 'Don't change the public signatures' it is at most a nit (borderline prohibition), not a block

evals.name: review-literal-filtering-R10
evals.prompt: Audit this prompt (target: opus). Prompt: 'Review this PR. Only report high-severity bugs and don't nitpick.'
assertions: Fires R10-review-literal-filtering at severity warn
Explains that a literal-following model obeys 'only high-severity' at the finding stage, dropping measured recall
Rewrite asks for full coverage with confidence + severity, moving filtering to a downstream step

evals.name: requires-tier-dependency-no-model
evals.prompt: Audit this prompt (no target model given): 'Refactor the billing service to be faster.'
assertions: Because no model is named, calls model-recommender to resolve the placement and tier before evaluating requires_tier rules
Then audits against that tier's profile (execution vs deliberation posture)
Fires R1/R5 (open-ended, no scope/acceptance) and rewrites with scope + verification

evals.name: delegation-model-unset-R12
evals.guards: Observed defect: four subagents inherited the escalation tier because the Agent call's `model` was left null.
evals.prompt: Audit this orchestrator prompt: "You are coordinating the migration. For each of the 9 packages, spawn a subagent with this brief: apply the codemod in scripts/codemod.ts to the package, run `pnpm -F <pkg> test`, and report pass/fail. Collect the results and summarize."
assertions: Fires R12-delegation-model-unset at block because the prompt establishes no effective selection source
Explains that resolution depends on definitions, defaults and the installed harness, rather than asserting all omitted parameters inherit
Rewrite establishes a matching agent definition or a supported explicit call value and marks actual execution unverified
Reapplies the consequence floor and verifier coverage before recommending lower capability

evals.name: handoff-assumes-carried-context-R13
evals.guards: A handoff exists to get an independent re-derivation; a brief that gestures at context the new session lacks cannot get one.
evals.prompt: Audit this handoff brief for a fresh session: "Take another look at the bug we discussed. The approach we tried before didn't work — the file you read earlier has the relevant handler. Same constraints as before. Figure out what we're missing."
assertions: Fires R13-context-assumed-not-carried at severity block
Identifies each unresolvable reference — 'we discussed', 'the approach we tried', 'the file you read earlier', 'same constraints'
Rewrite names files by path, restates the constraints and premises in full, and marks which premises are verified versus assumed
Does not merely soften the wording — it makes the brief self-contained

evals.name: self-contained-brief-not-flagged-control
evals.guards: R13 must not fire on a brief that legitimately references a file it names, or the rule becomes noise on every real handoff.
evals.prompt: Audit this handoff brief: "Investigate why `POST /bookings` returns 409 for same-day reservations. Verified: the 409 comes from `src/booking/conflict.ts:88`, and the overlap check uses local dates (see the test at `test/conflict.spec.ts:41`). Assumed but NOT verified: that the reservation timezone is always the fleet's. Constraint: do not change the public response shape. Read those two files first and say whether the assumption holds."
assertions: Does NOT fire R13 — every reference is named by path and each premise is labelled verified or assumed
Recognizes it as a well-formed investigation brief
Emits at most one or two minor findings and does not rewrite it wholesale

evals.name: named-agent-selection-is-valid
evals.prompt: Audit this delegation: use the named inventory-reader agent. Its inspected definition selects exactly the model mapped to recon; installed harness precedence has been checked, no overrides apply. The call omits model. Task: inventory the exported symbols in src/parser.ts; return paths and names only.
assertions: Does not fire R12 merely because the call omits model
Preserves the matching named-agent definition without forcing an override
Distinguishes verified configuration from observed execution

evals.name: override-does-not-prove-effective-target
evals.prompt: Audit this plan: call a named reviewer with the execution alias and claim execution-tier savings. Its definition pins the deliberation model, and this harness gives that definition precedence over call parameters.
assertions: Fires R12 for mismatch despite the explicit call parameter
Does not attribute execution-tier savings to the proposed run
Explains that the named definition controls the effective model here
